newsitem.title: UK: Feelgood factor returns for UK small cos - survey.
newsitem.headline: Feelgood factor returns for UK small cos - survey.

text.p: UK smaller companies are among the most optimistic in Europe, with firms' confidence in the economy, commercial prospects and employment levels far outstripping their French, German and Italian counterparts, a survey released on Monday showed.

They 3i European Enterprise Centre said its European Enterprise Index showed British and Spanish small and medium enterprises emerged as the most confident about commercial issues, with the majority expecting further improvement in 1997.

The survey by the UK centre is funded by investment firm 3i. It is conducted every six months among 8,000 small and medium sized enterprises in Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Spain. It was carried out in December.

The centre's main Enterprise Index comprises the Economy and Business Indices which reflect expectations for the next six months about the economy and other business issues, including performance, expenditure, investment and labour respectively.
The pan-European economy index remained negative, but the picture was improving, it said.

British and Spanish firms are also optimistic about their own performance, expecting to take on more staff, raise turnover and profit and to invest more on plant and equipment, IT, training and research and development.
The survey said managers in France, Italy and Germany all expect to see a decline in profitability and employment levels. Also, fewer firms in those countries expect to raise additional finance.
More firms in Britain expect to raise additional finance, while the amount looking to do so in Spain is unchanged.
But it said that even in countries where confidence in the economy is relatively low, managers are prepared to step up spending.
German managers expect to spend more on training, research and development and marketing, while French managers are prepared to invest further in plant and IT.
"It is pleasing to see a clear rise in the pan-European Economy Index but the differences in confidence between countries remains distinctly diverse," 3i marketing director Adam Quarry said.
